description: The recovery point objective is the maximum acceptable data loss, measured in time; the recovery time objective is the maximum acceptable time until the service is restored.
Active-passive keeps a standby region that is promoted during failover; active-active serves users from every region and must decide who writes each record.
The single region that takes every write for a record or partition, so two regions never change the same data concurrently.
Conflict resolution that keeps the write with the latest timestamp and silently discards the concurrent one.
A conflict-free replicated data type, such as a counter or a set, whose concurrent updates always merge to the same state on every replica.
A complete, independent copy of the workload that serves a subset of customers, reached through a thin router that maps a partition key to a cell.
Each customer gets its own combination of workers, so a poison customer fully affects only the few customers that share its exact combination.
Keeping the service running through an impaired dependency without making changes, using pre-provisioned capacity and the last known configuration instead of the control plane.
